analysis: Lumora Skin's vitamin C serum acquisition program acquired 873 new customers across the quarter, with paid channels (Meta, TikTok, Google) delivering 753 customers at 86 percent of new acquisition and owned channels (email, SMS) delivering 120 at 14 percent. The leaky bucket pattern is present and quantified: 90-day cohort tracking shows paid channels churning at 55 to 75 percent versus owned channels retaining 71 to 76 percent, a gap of more than 40 percentage points sustained across volume and value. TikTok carries the highest churn rate at 75 percent, meaning 126 of its 168 new customers do not return for a second order; at the channel's $22 first-order average order value this represents $2,772 of immediate second-order revenue not realized and $13,230 of lifetime value forgone when measured against the $145 annual customer value SMS produces. Meta carries a 68 percent churn rate at the highest absolute volume, churning 279 of 410 new customers; that single channel accounts for $6,696 of the immediate second-order revenue gap. The annual customer value to acquisition cost ratio for paid channels lands at 1.41x on a weighted basis ($53.20 annual value against $37.80 acquisition cost), well below the 3x healthy threshold; owned channels run at 16.6x against the same threshold, with SMS reaching 29x and email at 11.5x. The structural gap between owned and paid is consistent: owned-channel customers arrive with prior brand context and self-select into the replenishment cycle that drives the $96 annual customer value benchmark, while paid customers behave as one-and-done buyers. Across the full quarter, 501 paid-channel customers churn within 90 days, each forgoing an average $24 second-order revenue, producing approximately $12,500 of revenue at risk in the immediate next-purchase window alone.

root_cause_hypothesis.hypothesis: Paid channels acquire customers without the prior brand context that drives replenishment behavior in the skincare category; the post-purchase experience does not convert first-time paid buyers into the repeat cycle that owned-channel buyers self-select into at acquisition
supporting_signals: Owned-channel customers retain at 71 to 76 percent against paid-channel retention of 25 to 45 percent
Annual customer value gap of $97 between owned and paid customers despite identical product, pricing, and post-purchase fulfillment
TikTok and Meta, the lowest-intent paid channels, carry the highest churn rates
Google Ads, which captures higher purchase intent than social, retains better than social but still falls 14 percentage points below the worst owned channel
root_cause_hypothesis.confidence_rationale: Five-channel cohort comparison shows a consistent owned-versus-paid retention gap of 30 to 50 percentage points; the pattern holds across both volume and value metrics, isolating the variable to channel-driven customer intent at acquisition rather than post-purchase fulfillment quality
